ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: No arising is the claim that things do not come into birth or arise.
EvidenceBody: Chan records make it something to embody, awaken to, realize, and question, but they also refuse to identify it with dormant stillness or a secure place in which to settle. Yongjue Yuanxian gives the sharpest direct boundary. He rejects calling ‘the mechanism quiescent and not yet issuing forth’ no arising (指機寂未發謂之無生), then says that things do not arise from themselves, from another, jointly, or without a cause; when none of these four modes arises, there truly is no arising (諸法不自生，不他生，不共生，不無因生，四俱不生，則實無生). In the Yongjia encounter, Huineng asks why Yongjia Xuanjue does not embody no arising and comprehend what has no speed; Yongjia answers that embodiment itself is no arising and comprehension originally has no speed (何以體取無生，了無速乎；體即無生，了本無速). The Visvabhu Buddha section of the Compendium of the Five Lamps attributes a verse saying that mind is originally without arising but exists because of objects (心本無生因境有). Guxue Zhe asks for ‘a phrase of no arising’ (如何是無生底句), Foyin Zhiqing says one can realize it immediately and then asks the assembly whether they want to see it, Puan Yinsu says that once it is awakened to it is never mistaken, and Konggu Daocheng asks for its meaning before comparing it to vast empty space. Chushi Fanqi supplies the strongest recorded reversal: when the mind dwells in no arising, no arising itself is birth and death; he raises the staff and says, ‘this is not no arising’ (心住，無生即生死；拈拄杖，云：這箇不是無生). Longer phrases preserve the base wording but add their own lexical work. Yang Jie criticizes further talk of no arising (更說無生話); Huineng pairs no arising with no extinguishing (無生無滅); Liangshan Yuanguan banishes recognition into ‘the country of no arising’ and then calls that resting place dead water that holds no dragon; Chushi cites ‘endurance concerning no arising beneath the staff’ (棒下無生忍); and Guifeng Zongmi explicitly names the longer phrase ‘endurance concerning no arising’ (無生法忍). These families show how Chan loads and tests the words without turning every compound into evidence for a second bare-headword sense.

Family rows are explicitly marked and do not buy bare-headword depth. The inherited target ‘unborn’ remains an alternate and search alias, but ‘no arising’ is primary because the corpus's direct definition concerns denied modes of arising rather than gestational status. Predicate, abstract-noun, and question uses concern the same claim and do not warrant grammar-only senses. Personal names containing the graphs are excluded as names, not converted into a lexical sense; named Chan figures belong on the local roster.

DifferentThingTest.Reason: The complete cases were retested for incompatible referents; retained senses differ by referent, while grammatical or rhetorical variation stays within one sense.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Aliases preserve ordinary English lookup, close synonyms, and the principal corpus-facing wording without adding an interpretation.
ModifierControls: Headword-bearing compounds and modifiers were checked; they remain controls unless the complete case changes the referent.
FamilyControls: Neighboring family terms were checked and do not donate unsupported meaning to this headword.
